contract.purpose: Reverse-lookup registry of instruments. The point is not 'what does this script measure' -- the filename usually implies that, and usually implies too much. The point is `conditioned_on` and `cannot_answer`: what the instrument silently holds fixed, and which questions it is therefore structurally unable to answer no matter how many times it is run.
contract.rule: cannot_answer is mandatory and must name questions somebody could plausibly believe this instrument settles. An empty cannot_answer means the entry has not been thought through. Conditioning that is invisible in the output is the failure mode this registry exists to prevent: measure_anchor_recall applies the item cap before enumerating, so it reads as an oracle over placements when it is an oracle over placements *of the ten items the cap admitted*.

conditioned_on: MAX_POOL_ITEMS_EVALUATED: the cap is applied before enumeration
the legacy Cartesian generator, forced deliberately so recall is measured against a fixed reference
a single snapshot per invocation
cannot_answer: whether an item outside the cap had better placements
whether the cap should be larger
anything about which item should have been chosen
whether recall matters: recall 0.167 with best_score_regret 0.0 was measured on one snapshot

the generated candidate set, hence the item cap and the anchor generator
stratum inclusion probabilities (rows are an unequal-probability sample; use sampling_weight)
outcome: physical labels (rotation, d_xy, d_z, placed-safe, valid, included)
cannot_answer: the opportunity cost of items never entered into the search -- they produce no rows
the effect of the item cap
gate precision/recall over the whole candidate population; selected_* cells are conditioned on selection

conditioned_on: one trajectory per (config, arm, repeat) unless repeats are requested
wall-clock: the online policy is anytime and saturates its budget
cannot_answer: any effect smaller than its own run-to-run variance, which is config-specific and reaches 5 placed on b000-k40 with an identical binary (MEASUREMENT_AUDIT F3)
why an arm differs -- it reports outcomes, not divergence points
anything about Task A: these configs set optimize=false

whether a stand-in proxy tracks its official component: final_com_z and priority_clean_ratio have each been directionally falsified once against a submission pair, and only the shake proxy has ever agreed
any official component directly -- the bundled evaluator computes fill_score and num_placed_items only, so cog/stability/placement/soft are stand-ins measured by us, not scores

conditioned_on: one bundled source case (000)
the shipped PlacementCore, which the dry run replays -- so E_theta moves whenever the core moves
machine speed on the online half of the episode, though not on the offline order selection
cannot_answer: whether the result transfers to another case
whether the proxy is calibrated -- it is a relative selector only
whether the terminal invalid action would be fixed; both arms still end on one

conditioned_on: stride systematic sampling (release series exact at stride<=16; settled series sparse)
the enumerated candidate set, hence the item cap
cannot_answer: whether a graded state value would help if it were used to act -- this is observational, there is no knob on this axis
anything about states the policy never reaches

conditioned_on: episodes that ended; survivors contribute nothing
states reconstructed from observed settle AABBs, not the live state
cannot_answer: the rate at which a channel is survived -- the denominator is deaths, not attempts
whether a different action would have survived; it is a post-mortem, not a counterfactual

conditioned_on: the declared probe set: a fixed 5-item pool and one empty container
infinite deadline and a fixed attempt budget, deliberately, so it never reads machine speed
cannot_answer: semantic changes the probes do not exercise -- it already misses the offline/online risk gap, because the probe's winner is a settled candidate, and MIN_SUPPORT_RATIO 0.55->0.50, because the probe sits far from the threshold
anything about cores predating PlacementCore.rescue_choose
how large a change is, or whether it is an improvement: it reports difference, not distance

scripts/build_branch_labels.py.analysis_unit: state x sibling action, labelled by the FINAL episode outcome
conditioned_on: the sibling set reconstructed from the same candidate set at that state, so it inherits the item cap and the anchor generator
the shipped policy running free after the forced action -- the label is Y under THIS policy, not under an optimal continuation
one episode per invocation; branch points come from that single trajectory
prefix reproducibility, which is checked per state rather than assumed because the search is deadline-limited
cannot_answer: whether a better action existed outside the sampled siblings -- it labels the candidates it was given, not the reachable set
anything with a sample size worth acting on from one episode: 15 decided pairs is inside the measured noise floor for small differences
which board feature explains the outcome; it produces the label a board functional could be scored against, it does not fit one
counterfactuals under a different continuation policy
scripts/build_branch_labels.py.note: The first instrument on this repository that produces a long-horizon paired label. Every earlier board-value label was short-horizon and is known unusable: placed-to-go is confounded by step and volume, immediate settle survival is unrelated to option counts, and 95.2% of Q-band sibling pairs tie on any short-horizon outcome.

conditioned_on: one source multiset per invocation; permutations vary arrival order ONLY, holding content, class mix, total volume and difficulty fixed
sequential execution, because the search is deadline-limited
the two arms compared; it does not sweep
outcome: noise floor of the base arm
cannot_answer: generalisation across item mixes from a single source -- that needs a second source, and the first time it was run on one the effect did not transfer (item-cap-effect-is-source-dependent)
the optimum value of a knob: it compares two arms, so a knee needs several invocations
why an arm wins; it reports outcomes, not divergence points
anything about runtime variance: permutation estimates omega, not xi

conditioned_on: a fixed invented protocol: 0.3 g lateral in +-x and +-y, 60 steps each, 120 settle, inside saveState/restoreState
the container has NO LID, so an item may leave the opening; a lost item is charged as both shift and topple
cannot_answer: the official stability_score, or any absolute level -- the protocol magnitudes are invented, so only same-config arm comparisons carry meaning
force on an item: kinetic energy stands in for it
whether an arm difference is significant -- the one paired study (first-pass-256) reached no significant sign test on any shake axis

any single-run or single-case comparison: measured repeat-to-repeat spread on identical configs is 22.7% median for shake_max_shift, 74.6% for shake_peak_kinetic_energy, 42.9% for shake_items_shifted (n=20 cells)
effects below roughly 15-20% even pooled: at n~25 paired runs per arm the SE of the mean is still 8-15%

conditioned_on: uniform density, centre of mass at the diagonal intersection
coverage read from settled AABBs with CONTACT_TOLERANCE 0.02, so a thin gap can hide a cover and a corner touch can invent one
priority and soft are evaluated independently, matching the published rule
cannot_answer: the official cog_score: its normalisation is unpublished, so only direction is readable
even direction reliably -- on the death-band submission pair com_z IMPROVED (0.754 -> 0.704) while official cog fell 20.7 percent
cross-config comparison, per COG_CONTRACT shipped inside the payload
anything about priority routing on the development suite: neither source case has a priority container, so priority_misrouted is structurally always 0
the official placement_score direction -- local priority_clean_ratio fell 0.803 -> 0.575 while official placement_score ROSE 143.8 percent
single-count differences, which are within the AABB reading noise

tests/test_scenario_matrix.py.note: Audited 2026-08-03. Two assertions were weaker than their names: the pre-loaded test only excluded a placement within 1e-6 of a seated item's CENTRE (a 1 cm overlap passed), and test_two_containers_are_both_reachable asserted only that indices were in range, which passes when every action goes to container 0. Both were rewritten; the second was renamed because its docstring promised what it did not check.

look-ahead and policy timeout passed in; the matrix does not vary them
outcome: 7 configs covering 1/2 containers x shelf x pre-loaded x dedicated
cannot_answer: what the official evaluation actually poses -- the combinations are declared in the rules, their distribution is not public
anything about 80-item two-container scenes: it reuses the 41-item mix across two containers, which is a different difficulty
